coverage_diff.notes: Supersedes the same-ref (6359353) diff-scan written at harness 0.186.1: its four findings were independently re-verified against the clone and carried forward (re-ranked); one new high-severity finding added. Diff also contains partial remediation of baseline FIND-002 (ClusterRole narrowed: pods/configmaps/services/apps CRUD removed; cluster-wide secrets CRUD remains) and the fix attempt for FIND-001.

findings.title: Deletion paths run before the new namespace validation: fake-ProjectClaim finalizer path deletes arbitrary cross-namespace Secrets
findings.description: The FIND-001 remediation inserts ProjectClaim.Validate() into both reconcile paths, but in both cases the deletion branch executes BEFORE validation, and the deletion branch is exactly where the operator performs writes against the attacker-referenced secret. (1) Fake path: EnsureProjectClaimFakeProcessed (controllers/projectclaim/projectclaim_fake.go:84-121) calls EnsureFinalizer() at line 88 - before Validate() at line 101 - so even a claim that fails the new cross-namespace check still receives ProjectClaimFinalizer, guaranteeing a deletion reconcile. The DeletionTimestamp branch (lines 92-100) then calls DeleteFakeSecret() (lines 31-46), which does client.Get + client.Delete on Spec.GCPCredentialSecret.{Namespace,Name} verbatim - no namespace check - using the operator's cluster-wide secrets delete (deploy/cluster_role.yaml still grants delete on secrets in all namespaces). (2) Non-fake path: ReconcileHandler's operation list (controllers/projectclaim/projectclaim_controller.go:102-115) orders EnsureProjectClaimDeletionProcessed before the new EnsureProjectClaimValidated, and FinalizeProjectClaim -> EnsureCCSSecretFinalizerDeleted -> getCCSSecret (projectclaimadapter.go:264-276) reads the unvalidated Spec.CCSSecretRef and deleteFinalizer issues client.Update on that foreign secret, stripping the operator's deletion-protection finalizer from another tenant's CCS credential secret. This is the same ordering gap as the DeletionTimestamp skip in projectreference_controller.go:84 (see -002). The new Validate() therefore closes the create-time read path of baseline FIND-001 but leaves the delete-time write paths open.
findings.exploit_scenario: A principal with create/delete rights on projectclaims.gcp.managed.openshift.io in its own namespace (the operator's intended tenant interface) creates a ProjectClaim annotated FakeProjectClaim=true with spec.gcpCredentialSecret={namespace: <victim-ns>, name: <victim-secret>}. The first reconcile adds the finalizer (line 88, pre-validation) and then parks the claim in Error state via the new Validate(). The attacker deletes the claim; the deletion reconcile enters the fake branch before Validate and the operator deletes <victim-ns>/<victim-secret> with its cluster-wide RBAC - arbitrary cross-namespace Secret deletion (e.g. another tenant's GCP credential secret, breaking their cluster and destroying key material availability). Variant: a valid CCS claim is updated to point ccsSecretRef at another tenant's secret (update wedges the claim in Error but the finalizer is already present), then deleted - the operator strips CCSSecretFinalizer from the victim secret, removing its deletion protection while its GCP project still depends on it.
findings.recommendation: Enforce the namespace check at the sinks, not only in reconcile order: have DeleteFakeSecret() and getCCSSecret() refuse any secret reference whose namespace differs from the ProjectClaim's namespace (deletion-time cleanup of a previously-valid same-namespace ref is unaffected, so finalizers cannot wedge). Additionally move EnsureFinalizer after validation in the fake path, and prefer CRD-level CEL immutability/validation on gcpCredentialSecret.namespace and ccsSecretRef.namespace so invalid refs can never be persisted.
findings.confidence_reason: Verified directly in the clone at 6359353: operation ordering in ReconcileHandler and EnsureProjectClaimFakeProcessed, finalizer-before-validation at projectclaim_fake.go:88, raw use of the spec reference in DeleteFakeSecret (client.Delete) and getCCSSecret (client.Get + client.Update via deleteFinalizer), and the ClusterRole retaining cluster-wide secrets delete/update. Not exercised against a live cluster.

findings.title: ProjectReference.Validate is self-referential: forged ProjectReference in a tenant namespace still reaches cross-namespace CCS secret read
findings.description: The FIND-001 remediation adds ProjectReference.Validate() (api/v1alpha1/projectreference_types.go:99-106), which only checks Spec.CCSSecretRef.Namespace == Spec.ProjectClaimCRLink.Namespace — both fields live in the same attacker-supplied spec, so the check is satisfiable by construction. The manager watches cluster-wide (main.go:79-89 sets no cache namespace restriction) and Reconcile never pins req.Namespace to the operator namespace (operatorNamespace const at line 44 is used only for the non-CCS org-secret default). A principal able to create ProjectReference CRs in any namespace can set ProjectClaimCRLink.Namespace = CCSSecretRef.Namespace = <victim-ns>, pass Validate at line 85, and reach getGcpClient (line 97 -> 156-165), which calls util.GetGCPCredentialsFromSecret with the attacker-chosen namespace/name before any cross-check against a real ProjectClaim. Additionally, the deletion path (line 84: DeletionTimestamp != nil) skips Validate entirely but still executes getGcpClient, so even the self-referential check is bypassed on delete. Enforcement-sibling gap per the depth heuristic: the ProjectClaim path got a reconcile-order guard (EnsureProjectClaimValidated) but the equivalent guard on the ProjectReference path validates attacker-controlled data against attacker-controlled data. Nearest baseline finding: FIND-001 (this is the residual vector its fix does not close).
findings.exploit_scenario: An attacker holding namespace-scoped RBAC that permits creating projectreferences.gcp.managed.openshift.io in a namespace they control (a misconfigured tenant role, or any compromised controller with such grants) creates a ProjectReference with CCS=true, CCSSecretRef={namespace: victim-ccs-ns, name: gcp-secret}, ProjectClaimCRLink={namespace: victim-ccs-ns, name: victim-claim}. The operator, running with cluster-wide get on secrets (deploy/cluster_role.yaml), reads the victim's GCP service-account secret and constructs a GCP client from it with attacker-chosen GCPProjectID; subsequent reconcile operations act on GCP using the victim's credentials driven by attacker-controlled spec fields.
findings.recommendation: In ProjectReferenceReconciler.Reconcile, reject (or ignore) ProjectReference CRs whose req.Namespace != operatorNamespace, and/or restrict the manager cache for ProjectReference to the operator namespace. Validate CCSSecretRef against the namespace of the actually-fetched linked ProjectClaim (after Get), not against the CR's own ProjectClaimCRLink field, and perform that validation before getGcpClient on the deletion path too (or skip getGcpClient during finalizer-only teardown).
findings.confidence_reason: Code path verified end-to-end in the checkout (watch scope, missing namespace pin, validate-before-getGcpClient ordering, deletion skip); residual uncertainty is only whether any shipped RBAC actually lets a non-admin principal create ProjectReference CRs outside the operator namespace.

findings.title: Namespace-mismatch validation is reconcile-time only (no CRD CEL/webhook), leaving a mutation race window
findings.description: The new Validate() guards run inside the reconcilers (EnsureProjectClaimValidated in the projectclaim operations list; the pre-getGcpClient block in projectreference_controller.go:84-93) rather than at admission. Nothing in deploy/crds or a webhook rejects a bad spec at write time, so enforcement is eventually-consistent: a ProjectClaim can be created valid (passing validation, letting the operator create the ProjectReference and progress) and then have spec.gcpCredentialSecret.namespace / spec.ccsSecretRef.namespace mutated to another namespace. The claim controller will mark the claim Error on its next reconcile, but the projectreference adapter independently consumes r.ProjectClaim.Spec.GCPCredentialSecret.{Namespace,Name} (projectreference_adapter.go:620,647-663) to create/read the credential secret, and can observe the mutated value in the window before the claim controller flags it (or while claim state is already CReady, where VerifyProjectClaimPending ordering differs). Validation-by-status is also silently undone if a later reconcile path resets Status.State.
findings.exploit_scenario: A tenant with update rights on their own ProjectClaim creates it valid, waits for the ProjectReference to progress, then patches gcpCredentialSecret.namespace to a namespace they cannot read but where a same-named secret exists; if the projectreference reconcile consumes the mutated claim before the claim controller re-validates, the operator writes/reads GCP SA credentials against the attacker-chosen namespace.
findings.recommendation: Enforce the namespace-match invariant at admission: add CRD CEL validation rules (e.g. self.spec.ccsSecretRef.namespace == '' || self.metadata.namespace == self.spec.ccsSecretRef.namespace) or a validating webhook, and additionally re-check in the projectreference adapter immediately before each secret read/write rather than relying on claim Status.State.
findings.confidence_reason: Structural gap is certain (no CEL/webhook in the diff or tree); exploitability of the race window depends on reconcile interleaving that static review cannot time precisely.

findings.title: Validate() treats empty secret-ref namespace as valid instead of defaulting or rejecting it
findings.description: Both new Validate() methods skip the check when the namespace field is empty (projectclaim_types.go:102,107; projectreference_types.go:102). Downstream consumers pass the empty string verbatim into client.Get / NamespacedName (projectclaimadapter.go:267, projectreference_controller.go:160-165, projectreference_adapter.go:647-663, projectclaim_fake.go:19-35). With controller-runtime's cached client an empty namespace on a namespaced Secret lookup fails (informer keys are ns/name), so today this yields reconcile errors/requeue loops rather than a cross-namespace read — an availability/consistency defect and a fragile invariant, not a demonstrated bypass. If any future consumer defaults empty to the operator namespace (as getGcpClient's non-CCS branch does for its own default), the skip becomes a real read of the operator's namespace.
findings.exploit_scenario: A tenant sets ccsSecretRef: {name: gcp-secret} with no namespace; validation passes, the operator enters a persistent error/requeue loop on that CR (resource-churn nuisance), and the invariant 'validated implies safe to consume' silently does not hold for the empty case.
findings.recommendation: In Validate(), reject empty namespace on required secret refs, or explicitly default it to the CR's own namespace before the equality check (mutating default at admission is cleaner).
findings.confidence_reason: Empty-skip and verbatim consumption verified in code; concrete security impact today is low because empty-namespace Gets fail rather than widen scope.

findings.title: Dependency bump lands google.golang.org/grpc v1.81.1, below the v1.82.1 fix for GHSA-hrxh-6v49-42gf (CVSS 8.8)
findings.description: The diff bumps google.golang.org/grpc from v1.59.0 to v1.81.1 (go.mod:92, indirect). osv-scanner flags GHSA-hrxh-6v49-42gf / GO-2026-6061 (xDS RBAC authorization engine and HTTP/2 transport server vulnerabilities), fixed in v1.82.1. Reachability is doubtful: grpc arrives via the GCP client libraries and the operator acts only as a gRPC/HTTP client — it runs no gRPC server and no xDS — so the vulnerable server-side code paths are unlikely to be linked into an exposed surface. Reported low-confidence rather than dropped because the bump is in the changed manifest and one point release short of the fix. Companion facts, dismissed: golang.org/x/text v0.38.0 (GO-2026-5970 infinite-loop, fixed 0.39.0 — indirect, DoS-class, no identified untrusted-input parse path) and golang.org/x/crypto openpgp advisory (unmaintained-package notice, no fix, openpgp not imported by first-party code).
findings.exploit_scenario: Only material if a future change (or a linked library) starts serving gRPC/HTTP2 with this module version; then a remote peer could exercise the HTTP/2 transport server flaws.
findings.recommendation: Take grpc to >= v1.82.1 in the same dependency-update PR stream (go get google.golang.org/grpc@v1.82.1 && go mod tidy); pick up x/text v0.39.0 while there.
findings.confidence_reason: Advisory and version verified via osv-scanner against the changed manifest; no reachable server-side grpc usage found in first-party code, so real-world exploitability is speculative.
